record_type_quote: Oeberst et al. (2021) reversed autobiographical false memories using source and false memory sensitization. The present study aimed to replicate and extend their findings by addressing methodological issues. We conducted three suggestive interviews to implement false memories, then applied two countermeasures: source sensitization and false memory sensitization. Thirty-four of 63 participants developed false memories.

targets.authors: Oeberst, A., M. M. Wachendörfer, R. Imhoff, and H. Blank.
targets.title: Rich False Memories of Autobiographical Events Can Be Reversed.
targets.evidence_quote: Oeberst et al. (2021) reversed autobiographical false memories using source and false memory sensitization. The present study aimed to replicate and extend their findings by addressing methodological issues.
targets.outcome_quote: We replicated Oeberst et al. (2021)'s findings, using a more standardized interview procedure and blind interviewer for the source and false memory sensitization interviews. The source and false memory sensitization significantly reduced the false without influencing the true memory quality. However, we also showed that these results might be, at least partially, due to the chosen cut-offs of the memory classification, which might have inflated the present results.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly conclude that they replicated the original findings and fully replicated the result pattern. Cautions about potentially inflated classification effects and extension hypotheses do not override that overall verdict. They discuss possible measurement artifacts without establishing that the original claim is invalid, so the special flawed category is not applied.
